newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel confident of up to 2.5 pct '97 GDP growth.
newsitem.headline: Waigel confident of up to 2.5 pct '97 GDP growth.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel on Thursday reiterated that he was confident Germany's economy would grow as much as 2.5 percent next year, but warned that there would be little reprieve for the country's jobless.

Speaking to reporters in Bonn, Waigel said the government's plans to cut the so-called solidarity tax surcharge on income tax bills to 5.5 percent in 1998 would put an additional 7.5 billion marks in the pockets of consumers.
The solidarity tax, raised to finance the costs of German unification, is currently 7.5 percent.
